title: Tiny Crowds, Big Jobs
question: Are the microbes living around us mostly enemies?
hook: Microbes first became famous as disease-makers, yet most turn out to be helpers.
idea: Microbes live in communities, and most of them are beneficial, so a healthy microbiome matters for health.

beats.prompt: In the seventeenth century Antonie van Leeuwenhoek looks at dental plaque, mud and water through an early microscope. What does he find?

choices.label: Only lifeless grit and dust
choices.feedback: It tempts because nobody expected life there, but he found diverse bacteria, fungi and protozoa.

choices.label: Many kinds of tiny life, including clumped communities called biofilms
Only disease germs that need eliminating
choices.feedback: Infectious disease did become the earliest focus of research, but he studied diverse microbes and found biofilms.

beats.explain: The first microscopes revealed a hidden world of microorganisms, and Leeuwenhoek found biofilms, a first sign of microbes interacting in complex communities.

beats.prompt: Put these steps in microbiome history in order
items: Microbial ecology begins with Beijerinck and Winogradsky (end of the nineteenth century)
Whipps and colleagues define the microbiome (1988)
An international panel publishes a new definition (2020)
beats.explain: The sentences date these steps to the seventeenth century, the end of the nineteenth century, 1988 and 2020.

beats.prompt: Match each microbiome to what is said about it
pairs: Lives both inside and outside plant tissues
A key regulator of host physiology
May change how we understand animals adapting to change
beats.explain: Each host has its own microbial community, with a role in the host's physiology, ecology or adaptation.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong; which?
steps: Microbes were first noticed as causes of infectious disease.
So researchers focused on microbes as agents to eliminate.
Later work showed only a small proportion of microbes are tied to disease.
So the overwhelming majority of microbes must be harmful and need eliminating.
beats.explain: The same research showed the overwhelming majority of microbes are essential for ecosystems and beneficial to other organisms.
